scope: Explicit project memory, conservative historical raw-import quarantine, provenance invalidation, queue/cost isolation and compact archive UI

modelReview.coverage: One actual targeted design/development-snapshot review. Final fixes were independently inspected and regression-tested; no subsequent model approval is claimed.

findings.summary: Forgetting archived imports unnecessarily rebuilt active indexed knowledge.
findings.resolution: Archive-only deletion preserves generation and tasks, returns taskId:null/graphPurgePending:false and does not start a worker. Project deletion still forces graph cleanup.
evidence: hub/src/evolved/memoryImports.test.ts:forgetting only archived imports does not purge or requeue successful active knowledge

findings.summary: Potential mismatch between event serialization and stored-message provenance.
findings.resolution: Normal socket and web emissions use persisted StoredMessage content. The real SQLite reopen/from-message/event roundtrip regression preserves the exact source hash. Manual user:reference hashes are explicitly excluded from trusted raw-source comparisons. Arbitrary nonpersisted synthetic events are not an authorization source.

findings.summary: Late failed ingest could overwrite newer item state after cancellation or lease replacement.
findings.resolution: Transactional fail() requires running task, matching lease and current generation before changing task/item state. Cost receipts settle before the state transition. Late paid failure and stale-lease regressions pass.

findings.summary: Subscriber exception might interrupt message dispatch.
findings.resolution: EventPublisher.emit already catches each listener independently and broadcasts afterward.

findings.summary: Audit schema assumptions and exact classification need confirmation.
findings.resolution: EvolvedStore creates the required audit schema before MemoryService. Missing audit table skips migration; unsupported malformed schemas fail rather than classify without provenance. An independent read-only target dry run confirmed the exact conservative predicate and retained explicit-intake items.

findings.summary: A memory:write capability can forget a known archived item ID.
findings.resolution: Existing project-scoped deletion authority remains available for privacy/source cleanup. Archive reads remain human-only; archive-only deletion cannot start reindexing after F1. UUID knowledge does not bypass project authorization.

findings.summary: Archive must expose more than one page.
findings.resolution: Stable created_at/id ordering, bounded offset and 100-item pages; previous-page recovery after deleting the final item.

findings.summary: Unfiltered sources() might expose archived provenance through another API.
findings.resolution: Repository-wide caller inspection found only internal tests; public memory routes use filtered ledger reads. Source lifecycle methods intentionally retain archive visibility for actual source deletion.

webFocused.reportedBy: web owner after archive-only success-copy delta

checks: no horizontal overflow or page errors
browser.expectedConsoleWarning: Service worker intentionally blocked by fixture
browser.postBrowserDelta: Only the archive-deletion success message changed; targeted Web tests passed again.

limits: Strict provenance classification deliberately leaves ambiguous historical entries active instead of guessing.
Archive retains raw text and sources until explicit forget or source deletion; it is excluded from active knowledge and graph generation.
Existing failed/error items are not automatically retried by migration. Previously successful or still pending active work may rebuild under unchanged project permissions and budgets.
A source/image rollback to pre-fix code would ignore the archive flag and resume old automatic imports; no database restore or silent unarchive is part of this change.
This record does not assert deployment, provider-login validity, paid-inference success or a backup restore test.
